# opencode-git-trailer

Automatic commit attribution for [opencode](https://opencode.ai).

When opencode makes a git commit, it gets a trailer naming the model that made
it:

```
Fix timeout handling in the retry path

Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-GGUF
```

Commits you make yourself are never touched. The plugin rewrites opencode's
own `shell` tool calls and nothing else. It does not write to `~/.gitconfig`,
install a `prepare-commit-msg` hook, or set `commit.template`.

It registers no model-facing tools. Attribution is applied outside the model's
context, so it cannot be forgotten or skipped.

## Requirements

- opencode 2.0+ (this is a V2 plugin; V1 plugin implementations do not run in
  V2 and vice versa)
- git 2.32+ for `git commit --trailer`

## Install

```sh
opencode plugin add @tiuxo/opencode-git-trailer
```

Or declare it in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` to enable it everywhere:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["@tiuxo/opencode-git-trailer"]
}
```

### From source

The repository is public, so it can also be installed directly, with no
registry involved:

```sh
opencode plugin add 'git+https://git.tiuxo.com/brian/opencode-git-trailer.git#v0.2.1'
```

For a local checkout, symlink it into the global plugin directory, which is
scanned automatically and needs no config entry:

```sh
ln -s /path/to/opencode-git-trailer ~/.config/opencode/plugins/git-trailer
```

Or declare the path explicitly. Relative paths resolve against the config file
that declares them, so use an absolute path in the global config. Note that a
bare `"."` is **not** a path; opencode reads it as a package name, so a
self-referencing entry must be written `"./"`:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": ["/absolute/path/to/opencode-git-trailer"]
}
```

Restart the opencode service so it picks up the new plugin:

```sh
opencode service restart
opencode api get /api/plugin   # look for "id":"git-trailer","state":{"status":"active"}
```

Locations that were already active keep their previous plugin set, so a
restart is the reliable way to enable it everywhere at once.

## Usage

Run `/git-trailer` for current status, or:

| Command | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `/git-trailer on` / `off` | Enable/disable globally |
| `/git-trailer here on` / `off` | Enable/disable for the current project only |
| `/git-trailer here auto` | Clear this project's override, follow the global default |
| `/git-trailer auto` | Attribute to whichever model is active (default) |
| `/git-trailer set <text>` | Pin attribution to a fixed value instead of tracking the model |
| `/git-trailer key <Key>` | Change the trailer key (default `Assisted-by`) |
| `/git-trailer status` | Show the configuration and exactly what would be added right now |

Settings persist in opencode's plugin storage and survive restarts. Replies
are delivered as synthetic messages, so changing a setting never costs a model
turn.

### Kill switch

`OPENCODE_GIT_TRAILER=0` disables the plugin outright, overriding every stored
setting.

It has to be set on the process running the opencode **server**, because that
is where plugins execute. Prefixing the TUI will *not* work when a shared
background service is already running, because the variable never reaches it:

```sh
OPENCODE_GIT_TRAILER=0 opencode              # no effect with a background service
OPENCODE_GIT_TRAILER=0 opencode --standalone # works: private server
OPENCODE_GIT_TRAILER=0 opencode serve        # works: you own the server process
```

For the ordinary shared-service setup, use `/git-trailer off` instead.

### Attribution

By default the trailer value is the active model's ID, with any org prefix and
quantization tag stripped, so
`shikigami/unsloth/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-GGUF:Q4_K_XL` becomes
`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-GGUF`.

The model is resolved per session from the request that issued the commit, so
switching models mid-session attributes correctly, and a subagent running on a
different model is attributed to its own model rather than the parent's.

### Precedence

Enablement is resolved in this order, first match wins:

1. `OPENCODE_GIT_TRAILER=0`
2. The current project's override, if one is set
3. The global default

## How it works

`ctx.tool.hook("execute.before")` intercepts opencode's `shell` tool calls
before they run, and `--trailer 'Key: Value'` is spliced into any `git commit`
found in the command. The rewritten command is what you see in the TUI and
what the permission system checks, so nothing happens invisibly.

Rewriting a command you did not write is a good way to corrupt it, so the
parser is fail-open: anything it cannot handle confidently is left alone. A
missing trailer is cosmetic; a mangled `git commit` is not.

- `src/scan.ts` splits the command into top-level statements and tokenizes
  them, tracking quote state so a `;` or `&&` inside `-m "a; b"` is not a
  separator. `(...)`, `$(...)`, `${...}` and backticks are opaque.
- Heredocs are skipped rather than parsed: `<<`/`<<-`, quoted or unquoted,
  several queued on one line. The body is never tokenized, so a message
  containing `&&` or the words `git commit` cannot be misread as shell.
- `src/rewrite.ts` steps past wrapper prefixes (`env`, `exec`, `command`,
  `nice`, `nohup`, `timeout <duration>`) and `VAR=value` assignments, checks
  the command word is `git` or `*/git`, walks git's global flags, and requires
  the subcommand to be exactly `commit`.
- The trailer is spliced in at an offset in the original string, so existing
  quoting and spacing survive byte-for-byte.

It leaves the command untouched on unterminated quotes, parens or heredocs, an
unrecognized global git flag, `--help`, `--amend`, and commits already
carrying the same trailer key.

A `prepare-commit-msg` hook would avoid parsing entirely, but installing one
needs `core.hooksPath`, which overrides the repository's own hooks and would
disable husky, lefthook or pre-commit in every repo opencode touches. Git has
no "always append this trailer" config.

## Limitations

- **Commits inside `(...)`, `$(...)` or backticks are not rewritten.** Their
  contents are opaque; guessing at them risks corruption.
- **Git aliases are not recognized.** Only the literal `commit` subcommand
  matches, since resolving `git ci` would mean reading repo config.
- **`--amend` is skipped**, assuming the original commit already carries the
  trailer.
- **`-F <file>` contents cannot be inspected**, so a trailer already inside
  that file is not detected. Git's `addIfDifferentNeighbor` default usually
  prevents a duplicate anyway.
- **Unrecognized global git flags cause a skip**, because guessing whether an
  unknown flag consumes an argument means guessing where the subcommand
  starts. Likewise for wrappers: `timeout 150 git commit` works,
  `timeout --signal=KILL 10 git commit` does not.
- **Combined short flags are not decomposed.** `git commit -am "msg"` is
  rewritten, but its message is not checked for an existing trailer the way
  `-m` is.

## Development

```sh
bun install
bun test        # parser, settings, attribution, and command behaviour
bun run typecheck
bun run check   # both
```

Symlink the checkout into `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` (see
[Install](#install)) to run the working copy. Edits apply to locations loaded
after the change; `opencode service restart` applies them everywhere.

Install it only once, because opencode rejects duplicate plugin IDs. If the same
plugin is reachable from both `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` and a `plugins`
entry, the second copy fails with `Duplicate plugin ID: git-trailer` while the
first keeps working. Check with `opencode plugin list`.

There is no build step: opencode loads V2 plugins from TypeScript source.
`@opencode/plugin` is type-only, imported with `import type` and erased at
runtime, so the published package has no runtime dependencies.

### Releasing

Push a `v*` tag matching `package.json`. CI runs the checks, verifies the
packed tarball, and stages the release on npmjs:

```sh
npm version patch        # or minor / major
git push origin main --follow-tags
```

Granular tokens can only stage, so approval is manual:

```sh
npm stage list
npm stage approve <stage-id>
```

A tag that disagrees with `package.json` fails the build instead of shipping.

### Why `index.ts` is at the repository root

opencode resolves a local directory plugin by trying `<dir>/server` and
`<dir>/index` through `Bun.resolveSync`, without consulting `package.json`
`main`/`exports`. A plugin whose only entrypoint is `src/index.ts` resolves to
nothing and is dropped silently, with nothing logged.

Installs by package name do use `exports`, so the root `index.ts` is a
re-export and both resolution paths land on it.
